name: Texas

governingStatutes.name: Texas Workers' Compensation Act
governingStatutes.citation: Tex. Lab. Code Title 5, Subtitle A

administeringAgency.name: Texas Department of Insurance, Division of Workers' Compensation (TDI-DWC)

coverageScope.nonSubscriberNote: Texas is the only state allowing private employers to opt out entirely; non-subscribers lose exclusive remedy defense

benefitCategories.medical: All reasonable and necessary treatment; network requirements may apply
benefitCategories.temporaryIncomeDisability: 70% of wages (80% if wage <$10/hr) up to $1,111/week (2024); max 104 weeks
benefitCategories.impairmentIncomeBenefits: 70% of wages × 3 weeks per % impairment; max 401 weeks
benefitCategories.supplementalIncome: Available after IIBs if earning capacity reduced by 15%+
benefitCategories.lifetimeIncome: 75% of wages for catastrophic injuries; lifetime

workersCompensation.enforcementPowers: DWC audits; administrative penalties; referral for fraud prosecution
workersCompensation.penalties: Administrative penalties up to $25,000/day; criminal penalties for fraud

programs.name: No State Disability Insurance
programs.note: Texas has no state temporary disability insurance program
programs.alternatives: Private disability insurance; SSDI/SSI for long-term

programs.name: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families
programs.administeringBody: Texas Health and Human Services Commission

programs.name: Texas Medicaid
programs.eligibility: Low-income; did not expand Medicaid under ACA
programs.wcInteraction: WC primary for work injuries; Medicaid may cover non-work conditions

statutes.name: Texas Labor Code Chapter 21 (Texas Commission on Human Rights Act)
statutes.protections: Mirrors federal Title VII and ADA; disability discrimination prohibited

statutes.name: Texas Whistleblower Act
statutes.protections: Protection for reporting violations of law

civilRightsFramework.retaliationProhibitions: Retaliation prohibited for filing complaints or participating in proceedings

enablingStatutes.disability: No state TDI; Human Resources Code for assistance programs

delegatedBodies.agency: Texas Workforce Commission Civil Rights Division

tribunals.name: SOAH
tribunals.jurisdiction: State Office of Administrative Hearings (various agencies)

laborStandards.authority: Payday Law; Child Labor Law (limited labor protections)

civilRights.deadline: 180 days from violation (300 with EEOC worksharing)

occupationalSafety.authority: Texas is not a state plan state; OSHA covers private sector; no state OSHA for private

filingDeadlines.twcCrd: 180 days from discriminatory act (or 300 days with EEOC)
filingDeadlines.lawsuit: Within 60 days of TWC right-to-sue notice

evidentiaryStandards.appeal: Substantial evidence review on judicial appeal

judicialReview.wc: BRC → CCH → Appeals Panel → District Court (modified de novo)
judicialReview.civilRights: TWC investigation → Right to sue → District Court
judicialReview.eeoc: May file with EEOC simultaneously; federal court option

specialConsiderations.nonSubscriberSystem: Texas is unique—employers may opt out of workers' comp. Non-subscribers lose exclusive remedy defense and may be sued in tort. Many large employers (e.g., Walmart, Texas-based energy companies) historically used opt-out 'benefit plans.'
specialConsiderations.oilAndGasIndustry: Significant non-subscriber presence in oil/gas sector; special injury funds may apply
specialConsiderations.constructionRequirements: Public construction projects require WC coverage
